text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Federal government terminates oil production contract of U.S. company Ashland to protect national interest.
- Death toll in building collapse in Enugu, eastern Nigeria rises to 30 on Friday from 20 the day before.
- A British citizen is arrested over advance fee fraud popularly called "419" after the section of the criminal code dealing with fraud.
- Heavy rainfall during the week has pushed food prices down as traders sell off perishable goods cheaply.
- Opposition NADECO group faults intelligence report that says it was planning to cause mayhem on Thursday, the fourth anniversary of the annulled June 12 1993 presidential election.
- National Electoral Commission may need five billion naira to conduct the elections needed to restore full democracy in Nigeria next year.
- Military administrator of southwestern Oyo state, Colonel Ahmed Usman, on Friday caught policemen on a special anti-crime assignment with money allegedly extorted from motorists.
- The government of Kano state in northern Nigeria requests for development assistance from Israel.

- Exiled opposition activist and Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka warns that a radical wing of Nigerian pro-democracy activists may emerge and begin a violent struggle to resolve the crisis over the annulment of a 1993 presidential election.
- Blue chip stocks suffer as wind of losses blows through the Nigerian stock market.
